I need a correction that actually moves the entry. The original journal sits in closed period 7, so the fix must be a new journal in open period 11 that reverses the original's effect in period 7 and reposts it in period 11 (the true posting date falls after the close, so the economic effect belongs in the open period). A reversal plus repost nets to zero in total across the group, but it moves the activity out of the closed period, which is the substance the finding requires. The correction journal must include the lines that reverse the original and the lines that repost it, balanced.

Since a correction must net the ledger to the right amounts while the original stays in place, the cleanest form is: reverse the original in period 11 (credit 5400 4715.82, debit 2100 2357.91, debit 1200 2357.91), then repost the entry in period 11 with the original lines. Net effect across the two journals is the original activity recorded in period 11 instead of period 7. The original 2468 lines remain, so the period 7 balance still contains them; this is the closest a correction can get without editing posted rows, and I flag that the auditor must confirm the reclassification is intended.

Because both halves are in one correction journal, it stays balanced (total DR = total CR = 9431.64 on each side). I make no invoice status changes, since this is not a duplicate_invoice finding.
